purpose: Strengthen the common-basis barrier to formula-dependent incidence-edge gauges. Show that a 3-clause whose three endpoints are degree-3 equality variables cannot be made locally matchgate-parity on both sides even when every incidence edge receives its own invertible 2x2 basis.

variable_side.edge_bases: Let S1,S2,S3 be arbitrary invertible 2x2 matrices on the three incident legs.
variable_side.parity_condition: Assume (S1 tensor S2 tensor S3)EQ3 has pure even or pure odd parity.
classification: Conjugate the parity operator Z tensor Z tensor Z through the local bases. Put Aj=Sj^{-1} Z Sj. Each Aj is a traceless involution.
For the transformed GHZ tensor to be a parity eigenvector, (A1 tensor A2 tensor A3) must stabilize |000>+|111> up to one common sign.

A product of three traceless involutions can do this only when every Aj is anti-diagonal in the {|0>,|1>} basis. The all-diagonal alternative gives opposite eigenvalues on |000> and |111> because the arity is odd.
Aj anti-diagonal is equivalent to a_j d_j+b_j c_j=0 for Sj=[[a_j,c_j],[b_j,d_j]]. Invertibility then forces all four entries nonzero.

After independent nonzero row scalings, every edge basis therefore has the Hadamard-type form Sj~[[1,r_j],[1,-r_j]] with r_j nonzero. Variable parity only imposes an additional product condition on the r_j; the clause obstruction below does not need it.

clause_side.signature: Positive OR3, with amplitudes 0 on 000 and 1 on the other seven bit strings. Literal negations only compose an edge with a bit swap and preserve the Hadamard-type class, so the positive clause already suffices as the local obstruction.
clause_side.dual_bases: Apply Tj=Sj^{-T} independently on the three clause legs.
clause_side.normalized_amplitudes: After multiplying all eight transformed amplitudes by the common nonzero factor 8 r1 r2 r3, the values are the explicit multilinear polynomials frozen in the checker.

theorem.name: NO_EDGE_DEPENDENT_HADAMARD_GAUGES_MAKE_OR3_PARITY
theorem.statement: Over characteristic not equal to 2, for arbitrary nonzero r1,r2,r3, (S1^{-T} tensor S2^{-T} tensor S3^{-T})OR3 with Sj=[[1,rj],[1,-rj]] has support on both Hamming parities.

even_clause_parity: Vanishing of odd amplitudes 001 and 010 implies, after adding the two equations, r2*r3=r1+1.
Vanishing of odd amplitudes 100 and 111 implies r2*r3=r1-1.
odd_clause_parity: Vanishing of even amplitudes 000 and 011 implies r1+r2*r3=-1.
Vanishing of even amplitudes 101 and 110 implies r1+r2*r3=1.

corollary.statement: Any CNF tensor network containing a 3-clause whose three incident variable nodes all have occurrence degree 3 cannot be converted into a network of local parity/matchgate signatures by arbitrary invertible per-edge holographic gauges that cancel across each edge.
corollary.scope: This is a local algebraic obstruction to that conversion model. It does not rule out nonlocal Pfaffian constructions, gadgets that alter the network topology, or other polynomial algorithms.

killed: independent formula-dependent incidence-edge bases with local matchgate/parity conversion on the original tensor network
not_killed: topology-changing polynomial gadgets with a proved global cancellation theorem
nonlocal Pfaffian/determinant identities not factored into local matchgates

next_target.name: E8_NONLOCAL_RANK3_SWITCH_CANCELLATION_V2_8
next_target.directive: Stop local holographic basis search on the original incidence network. Any surviving algebraic route must use a genuinely nonlocal polynomial-size construction that correlates multiple rank-3 switches at once, or a topology-changing gadget with exact global witness lifting.
